Today you will discover the rare and breathtaking beauty of Perito Moreno Glacier, one of Argentina's natural treasures and part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
In the morning, your guide will collect you from your hotel for a full-day excursion to Perito Moreno Glacier.
On the way to the national park, your guide will explain the glacier's significance and share interesting facts and details about this remarkable natural site.
The first stop is a network of walkways and viewing platforms offering magnificent glacier views and opportunities for memorable photographs.
The bus then continues through the park, giving you time to enjoy the scenery and natural beauty of Patagonia.
You can walk along the designated paths, admire the glacier from different angles and witness the spectacular natural phenomenon of calving, when enormous blocks of ice break away and crash into the water.
At the end of the day, return to your hotel by bus.

The Andean Candelabra is a giant drawing on a hillside in a bay on the Paracas Peninsula. It stands about 130 meters high and measures about 75 meters across. The design is visible from both the sea and the air. Many legends surround its origins, and one theory connects it with the symbol of the "tree of life."

The boat then heads to the Ballestas Islands, a group of 3 large islands and numerous small rocky islets with grottoes and arches.

Penguins, sea lions, fur seals and many birds live here. Landing on the islands is prohibited, so visitors see them from the water. Dolphins occasionally approach the shores.

After the boat excursion, you will head to the airfield for a flight over the Nazca Desert.

From the air, you can see enormous images of humans and animals, including a monkey, hummingbird and spider, as well as geometric figures.

The flight lasts 35 minutes.

After landing, return to Lima and transfer to your hotel.

The Paracas–Nazca day brings together 3 very different experiences. First, you see the Andean Candelabra from the sea; then the boat passes rocky islands with sea lions, fur seals, penguins and birds. Finally, the route moves into the desert, where only from the air can you appreciate the scale of the Nazca Lines and distinguish individual figures and geometric patterns.
